title: Typed output circuit-breaker and constrained-decode failure-injection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Build a reproducible, cross-model smoke and stress suite that exercises constrained decoding + streaming JSON mode under intentional failure modes and validate circuit-breaker behavior for typed outputs. This ticket implements harness additions to inject token-loss, truncated-streams, interleaved toolcall tokens, and KV-cache misalignments while asserting schema adherence and safe fallback policies. Deliverables: (1) deterministic failure-injection harness for streaming, (2) a set of canonical test scenarios and golden traces, (3) circuit-breaker and backoff assertions in the CI matrix, and (4) a runbook for observed failure classes and mitigation recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Test harness can inject and replay at least 6 failure classes deterministically across two model families (open-llama-65b, redwood-rlhf-7b).
A2: Constrained decoder enforces schema for 95% of non-adversarial streams and triggers fallback to lax-parser or toolcall-retry within 200ms for remaining cases in CI runs.
A3: Streaming aggregator recovers from a truncated chunk scenario and emits a partial-recovery telemetry event that matches the golden trace format.
A4: Circuit-breaker trips and routes to fallback model variant (quantized or smaller) under sustained schema-violating outputs with >10% anomaly rate, as verified by an automated canary test.
A5: Playbook and links to test artifacts and failing traces are published to Confluence and linked from the test failure dashboard.
test_plan: Matrix across model variants: open-llama-65b, redwood-rlhf-7b, llama-2-13b (quantized and fp16 runs).

Failure classes: (F1) dropped tokens mid-stream, (F2) token duplication, (F3) interleaved toolcall tokens, (F4) truncated final chunk, (F5) KV cache desync across multi-step calls, (F6) adversarial prefix that looks like close-brace.
Decoder asserts: schema strictness levels 0..3; measure false-positive and false-negative enforcement rates per model/level.
Circuit-breaker thresholds: anomaly windows 1m/5m/15m and trip conditions configurable via runtime flags.
Telemetry: emit typed events for "partial_parse", "schema_violation", "fallback_trigger", and attach raw chunked traces for offline debugging.
harness_steps: 1) Extend stream-replayer to support drop/dup/truncate operations at byte offsets and token boundaries.
2) Add an 'interleave-toolcall' mode that inserts toolcall markers and checks tool-return schema collisions.
3) Wire failure-injection flags into CI runner matrix and add a non-flaky gating job marked 'structured-output-smoke'.
4) Implement additional telemetry tags (scenario, injected_failure, model_variant, decode_level) and forward to the streaming traces pipeline.
5) Add golden-trace comparator that verifies emitted telemetry + recovered payload against expected canonical traces.
6) Document mitigation runbook and add example CLI for reproducing failing traces locally.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Failure injection may increase CI flakiness and noise. Mitigation: run heavy failure scenarios in a separate nightly gating job and keep minimal smoke cases in PR presubmit.
Risk: Telemetry volume from raw traces could spike storage. Mitigation: sample 1/10 traces for full raw payload and keep full traces only on failure windows.
Risk: Model variability causes non-deterministic decode outcomes. Mitigation: pin sampling/temp to deterministic settings for CI; measure variance separately in an exp bucket.
Risk: Security sensitivity of toolcall traces. Mitigation: scrub API keys and PII from replayed traces before storing; add KMS-encrypted artifact bucket for full traces.
notes: Design decision: prefer graceful fallback (lax-parser + scoring) over aggressive token-level corrections to avoid hallucinated structure fixes.
We will reuse existing streaming-assertor hooks from ENG-911337 and extend to emit structured-output-specific events.
Prototype PR 1287 contains the initial replayer and a simple truncated-stream scenario used during spike testing.
Follow-up epics: split heavy adversarial fuzzing into a separate project once core harness stabilizes.
